candidates.title: Fix homepage Lighthouse CI perf: 0.76 → 0.80+
candidates.why: Lighthouse CI has been red across every push since S209 (2026-06-19), consistently scoring 0.76 on the homepage against a 0.80 threshold. The failure blocks release confidence CANON-007 staging gate and the doctor's 'Launch readiness' advisory. Root causes identified: `supabase-public.js` loads without `defer` (sole blocking external script), 25+ deferred scripts all executing together post-DOMContentLoaded driving Total Blocking Time above the orange threshold, and possible CLS from the async CSS (print→all) swap if shell CSS rules override inline critical CSS above the fold.
candidates.recipe: 1. Add `defer` to `supabase-public.js` in index.html (propagate-nav will pick it up for other pages); 2. Audit the 25 deferred scripts — move non-critical ones (vault-resonance, vault-pulse, ignis-tour, recent-ships, pwa-install) to `requestIdleCallback` / IntersectionObserver lazy-load instead of immediate defer; 3. Run check-perf-budget after changes and re-run the local preview + LHCI.

L1.recipe: Add defer to supabase-public.js in index.html (propagate via propagate-nav to all pages) — removes the only parser-blocking external script.

L2.recipe: L1 + move 5 non-critical deferred scripts to idle/intersection-triggered loading so they don't pile onto the post-DOMContentLoaded execution burst.

L3.recipe: L2 + add a script scheduler that measures the main-thread load and budgets each script's init, ensuring no single run-to-completion task exceeds 50ms TBT.

candidates.evidence: gh run list --workflow 'Lighthouse CI' shows 8 consecutive failures; log: found 0.76 vs expected >=0.80; grep 'supabase-public' index.html confirms no defer attribute on line 2388

candidates.title: IGNIS oracle answer quick-rate: 👍/👎 inline feedback loop
candidates.why: IGNIS answers are generated by a prefix-match index against 65+ docs but there is no signal on whether answers are actually useful to visitors. Without a quality feedback loop, the oracle has no learning surface — improvements are guesswork. A lightweight 👍/👎 rating appended to every oracle answer response would generate the first closed-loop quality signal and directly inform which queries need better index coverage.
candidates.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js: after rendering the oracle answer container, append a 2-button rating row (👍 / 👎) styled with the existing theme tokens. On click: emit oracle:answer_rated RUM event with the query and rating; store locally to suppress re-display; hide the rating row. Add oracle:answer_rated to Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS. No server storage required — RUM accumulates the signal.

L1.recipe: Add 👍/👎 buttons to oracle answer; RUM oracle:answer_rated:{query_slug}:{up|down}; Worker allowlist update.

L2.recipe: L1 + store rating in localStorage so same-session repeats don't re-show; show a 'Thanks' micro-animation on rate.

L3.recipe: L2 + build a rollup script that aggregates oracle:answer_rated RUM into a per-query quality table (top/bottom rated queries) surfaced in the IGNIS admin or a new api/oracle-quality.json feed.

candidates.evidence: grep oracle:answer_rated assets/ignis-answer-engine.js returns no match — feature does not exist; Worker RUM_UX_EVENTS in scripts/worker-lib.mjs has no oracle:answer_rated entry

candidates.title: Load non-critical deferred scripts via requestIdleCallback/IntersectionObserver
candidates.why: The homepage loads 25+ deferred scripts that all fire their init code in a burst after DOMContentLoaded. Even with defer, this batched execution causes a TBT spike that is likely the primary driver of the 0.76 Lighthouse score. Scripts like vault-resonance.js, vault-pulse.js, ignis-tour.js, pwa-install.js, and cookie-consent.js are only relevant in specific conditions (signed-in state, scroll position, browser capability). Lazy-loading them via requestIdleCallback or IntersectionObserver reduces main-thread contention at the critical measurement window.
candidates.recipe: Create a micro-loader wrapper in ambient-loader.js or a new lazy-init.js (predicate-loaded): for each non-critical script, replace the static defer tag with a dynamic `document.createElement('script')` appended in `requestIdleCallback(() => { ... })`. Candidate non-critical scripts: vault-resonance, vault-pulse, ignis-tour, recent-ships (below fold), pwa-install (capability check first), cookie-consent (below fold). Keep critical path scripts as static defer.

L1.recipe: Move 3 clearly non-critical scripts (ignis-tour, vault-resonance, vault-pulse) to requestIdleCallback loading in index.html. Propagate via propagate-nav.

L2.recipe: L1 + build a lightweight lazy-init.js orchestrator that defers 8+ scripts by category (engagement, portal, analytics) with configurable priority hints.

L3.recipe: L2 + add TBT budget enforcement: each idle-queued script records its own execution time via performance.mark; if budget (50ms) is exceeded, delay remaining queue by 100ms.

candidates.evidence: curl http://127.0.0.1:4173/ | grep '<script' shows 25+ scripts, only supabase-public.js without defer; Lighthouse CI scores 0.52/0.76/0.76 with median 0.76 (TBT most weighted metric at 30%)
